props.title: Little Big Man
props.initialSlug: A boy raised by Indians survives the Wild West

sections.content: Little Big Man revolutionized the Western genre by flipping the traditional "cowboys and Indians" narrative on its head. Through Dustin Hoffman's masterful performance as Jack Crabb, the 121-year-old sole white survivor of Custer's Last Stand, the film presents one of the first sympathetic portrayals of Native Americans in mainstream cinema. Unlike John Ford's The Searchers (1956) or Stagecoach (1939), director Arthur Penn shows the genocide of Native Americans through a critical lens, particularly in the devastating Sand Creek Massacre sequence. The film's influence can be seen in later revisionist Westerns like Dances with Wolves (1990) and Dead Man (1995).

sections.content: The film's satirical approach to American mythology was groundbreaking for 1970. Coming during the Vietnam War era, Little Big Man draws clear parallels between the genocide of Native Americans and contemporary military actions. This influenced later films like Soldier Blue (1970) and Ulzana's Raid (1972) that used the Western genre to comment on Vietnam. Chief Dan George's portrayal of Old Lodge Skins marked a crucial shift away from white actors playing Native Americans, as seen in films like Broken Arrow (1950).

The film's structure - spanning decades of American history through one man's story - influenced epic historical dramas like Forrest Gump (1994). Its blend of comedy and tragedy, particularly in depicting historical atrocities, created a template for films like The Ballad of Buster Scruggs (2018). The movie's questioning of American historical narratives paved the way for revisionist Westerns like Unforgiven (1992) and The Power of the Dog (2021). sections.content: Little Big Man marked a turning point in Hollywood's portrayal of Native Americans. The film's influence can be seen in later works like Thunderheart (1992) and Smoke Signals (1998), which continued to challenge stereotypical depictions. The character of Old Lodge Skins, with his dignity and humor intact despite facing genocide, created a template for complex Native American characters that influenced films like Wind River (2017) and Hostiles (2017).
